summary: Intermittent p99 latency on identical repeat-turns due to prefix cache TTL fragmentation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer running conversational micro-threads is observing intermittent p99 latency spikes (~2-4s) on otherwise identical repeat user turns. The slow turns are reproducible when the same prompt is replayed in quick succession but only for a subset of conversation IDs.

Impact:
- Customer (Acme Payments, dedicated) sees ~1-2% of requests hitting p99 ~2-4s for short repeat-turn prompts; p50 remains ~60-120ms.
- Affects production traffic in us-east region for dedicated pool causing degraded UX for high-frequency bots.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (dedicated pool), prod us-east
- Model: o4x-heavy-8k serving pinned version v2026-02-10
- Client traffic pattern: many short user turns (5-20 tokens) with repeated identical follow-up prompts in quick succession.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use Acme test harness that replays a canonical follow-up prompt every 200ms for 1000 sessions pinned to the same model/version.
2) Observe latency distribution per session; most sessions p50 ~60-120ms, but ~1-2% sessions show spikes to 2-4s at unpredictable intervals.
3) Correlate request IDs from slow responses to kvcache miss log and prefix-lookup fallback traces.

Observed metrics & logs:
- kvcache.prefix_lookup_miss_rate (shard-level) increases in tandem with p99 spikes (Grafana dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-cache/ttl-fragmentation).
- kvcache.eviction_count shows small bursts on specific shards that align with spikes.
- Traces show requests go to cold-path (full KV fetch + backfill) and take ~1.8-3.4s extra for token 1-5.
- Logs: "kvcache: prefix mismatch on shard s-17 for key tenant:acme:conv:xxxx" followed by a backfill call to redis/nebula.

Preliminary hypothesis:
- Tenant-specific variability in prefix TTLs (some prompt prefixes are assigned shorter TTLs by an adaptive policy) combined with shard-aligned eviction causes fragmentation: identical prompts sometimes land on a shard where the prefix was recently evicted or had a very short TTL, forcing cold-path lookups.
- Prefetch/warmup for some shards is rate-limited and the backfill path competes with other recovery work, amplifying latency when a shard experiences repeated short-lifetime entries.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Increased kvcache.prefetch_concurrency for the affected dedicated pool to reduce backfill queueing (rolled to Acme pool at 2026-03-13T21:12Z).
- Deployed short-term TTL floor (min_prefix_ttl = 15s) for conversation prefixes in Dedicated pools to reduce fragmentation (feature flagged).

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: run targeted simulations replaying Acme workload to reproduce deterministic shard eviction sequence (owner: Marco Rivera).
- Runtime: instrument per-key TTL histograms and shard-level prefetch queue latency (owner: Priya Menon).
- Product: evaluate permanent config options for per-tenant TTL floors or adaptive warmup for high-frequency tenants (owner: Luis Ortega).
- CS: inform customer of mitigation and monitor for improvement over next 24h (owner: Ayesha Khan).

Owner: Marco Rivera (SRE)
Priority: P1 (customer-facing latency affecting product UX)
